about.description: Built on Tauri 2 + React + CodeMirror 6, Quill is a local-first Markdown editor. It integrates AI chat, desktop pet, plugin system, ER diagrams, schedule management, and CLI tools — your data stays on your device in standard Markdown, no lock-in.

philosophy.label: Philosophy
philosophy.localFirst: Local-first — your notes belong to you. All documents are stored as plain Markdown files on your local filesystem, no cloud account required, fully usable offline, free to migrate. The Vault system supports pluggable backends via the vault-provider abstraction layer, but data ownership always stays with you.
philosophy.openFormat: Open format — no lock-in. Quill uses standard Markdown as its only storage format, processed by the remark/rehype pipeline for GFM and custom directives. Any text editor can open your notes; export to HTML locally or hosted to remote storage anytime; after uninstalling Quill, your data remains fully readable.
philosophy.extensible: Extensible — open end-to-end, from editor core to storage backends. The microkernel + plugin SDK supports 14 container directives (callout, tabs, mermaid, etc.) and third-party plugins; the CLI adapter abstraction makes 6 AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Opencode, Pi, Qoder) pluggable; pnpm workspaces lets container-plugins, vault-provider, cli-adapter, plugin-host, and plugin-sdk evolve as independent packages.
philosophy.privacy: Privacy-first — AI chat and code generation flow through local CLI tools; your API keys and conversation content never touch Quill's servers. CSP policy and the plugin sandbox tier provide defense-in-depth, with trusted and sandbox tiers executing separately; third-party plugins run under restricted permissions.

projectStructure.label: Project structure
projectStructure.description: Quill is a pnpm monorepo — the desktop app, CLI adapter, container plugins, Vault Provider, and Plugin Host/SDK are each independent packages.
projectStructure.tree:
quill/
├── apps/
│   └── desktop/              # Tauri desktop app
│       ├── src/              # React frontend
│       │   ├── components/   # UI components (shell, editor, AI, sidebar, etc.)
│       │   ├── editor/       # CodeMirror extensions
│       │   ├── hooks/        # React hooks
│       │   ├── store/        # Zustand stores
│       │   └── utils/        # Utility modules
│       └── src-tauri/        # Rust backend (Tauri commands)
├── packages/
│   ├── cli-adapter/          # AI CLI adapter abstraction (Claude/Codex/Gemini/Opencode/Pi/Qoder)
│   ├── container-plugins/    # Markdown container directive plugins (14)
│   ├── vault-provider/       # Vault storage provider abstraction
│   ├── plugin-host/         # Plugin host runtime
│   ├── plugin-sdk/          # Plugin development SDK
│   └── create-quill-plugin/ # Scaffold tool
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
└── tsconfig.base.json

storage.title: Storage & Sharing
storage.description: Cloud object storage — used for image hosting and HTML sharing

r2.publicHint:
Make the bucket public-read (R2 → Settings → Public Development URL, or bind a custom domain). Uploaded objects return 403 until you do.
R2 image host domains are NOT in the CSP baseline — if image previews don't render, add the domain to Settings → Security Policy.
You also need a CORS rule on R2 → Settings → CORS Policy: AllowedOrigins must include tauri://localhost, http://tauri.localhost and http://localhost:1420; AllowedMethods must include PUT; AllowedHeaders must include authorization, x-amz-content-sha256, x-amz-date and content-type. Without it, browser uploads fail at preflight with 403.

qiniu.publicHint:
Bind a custom domain in Qiniu console and set bucket to public-read. Uploaded objects return 403 until you do.
The default http://*.clouddn.com test domain is baseline-allowed; if you bind a custom domain and previews don't render, add it to Settings → Security Policy.

oss.publicHint:
Set the bucket ACL to public-read (OSS → Bucket → Permissions → Bucket ACL = public-read), or bind a custom domain in the console. Uploaded objects return 403 until you do.
The OSS baseline https://*.aliyuncs.com is in the CSP allow-list; if you bind a custom domain and previews don't render, add it to Settings → Security Policy.
You also need a CORS rule on OSS → Bucket → Data Security → Cross-Origin: AllowedOrigin must include tauri://localhost, http://tauri.localhost and http://localhost:1420; AllowedMethod must include PUT; AllowedHeader must include authorization, x-oss-date, x-oss-content-sha256 and content-type. Without it, browser uploads fail at preflight with 403.
